title: LFU Cache
description:
Design and implement a data structure for a Least Frequently Used (LFU) cache.

Implement the LFUCache class:

LFUCache(int capacity) initializes the object with the capacity of the data structure.

int get(int key) gets the value of the key if the key exists in the cache. Otherwise, returns -1.

void put(int key, int value) updates the value of the key if present, or inserts the key if not already present. When the cache reaches its capacity, it should invalidate and remove the least frequently used key before inserting a new item. For this problem, when there is a tie (i.e., two or more keys with the same frequency), the least recently used key would be invalidated.

To determine the least frequently used key, a use counter is maintained for each key in the cache. The key with the smallest use counter is the least frequently used key.

When a key is first inserted into the cache, its use counter is set to 1 (due to the put operation). The use counter for a key in the cache is incremented either a get or put operation is called on it.

Both get and put must run in average O(1) time complexity.

examples.explanation: With capacity 2: put(1,1) and put(2,2) fill the cache. get(1) returns 1 and raises key 1's frequency. put(3,3) evicts key 2 (frequency 1, the least frequently used), so get(2) returns -1. get(3) returns 3. put(4,4) evicts key 1 (both keys now share the lowest frequency, and key 1 is least recently used), so get(1) returns -1, get(3) returns 3, get(4) returns 4.

constraints: At most 2 * 10^5 calls will be made to get and put.
approach: Keep a key map for direct value and frequency lookup, plus one ordered bucket per frequency whose iteration order captures recency among keys sharing that count. A get or updating put moves the key from its current frequency bucket to the next one; if the emptied bucket was the minimum, the minimum frequency advances by one. Track min_frequency so eviction never scans: on an insertion at capacity, drop the oldest key in the minimum-frequency bucket (least frequent, and among ties least recent). A new key enters with frequency 1 and resets min_frequency to 1. Hash-map and ordered-bucket edits are all constant time, so each operation is average O(1).
